features.definition: The complete NV_NVDLA_csb_master root has84 native ports and no top parameters. Falcon-side request acceptance and final response outputs use rising nvdla_falcon_clk and asynchronous active-low nvdla_falcon_rstn. Request dispatch,client response capture and response ingress use rising nvdla_core_clk and asynchronous active-low nvdla_core_rstn. The clocks are independent and may pause; timing is determined by their actual edge history,including coincident edges using pre-edge state. There are14 clients in this numeric order:cfgrom,glb,mcif,cdma,csc,cmac_a,cmac_b,cacc,sdp_rdma,sdp,pdp_rdma,pdp,cdp_rdma,cdp. Request RAM has4 records of50 bits; response RAM has2 records of34 bits. Both channels have one additional input staging record. The fixed functional build uses FPGA,NO_PLI,PRAND_OFF,real low-phase-latched clock enables and no power-clock bypass. No random FIFO-stall or FIFO-depth override is applied. pwrbus_ram_pd has no functional effect in this build. The independent model uses the same84 ports with no formal parameters or external macro requirement.

features.definition: Apply the following rule independently to each FIFO channel at its writer clock,with depth D=4 for requests or D=2 for responses. Track a pending input bit P,internal full/busy bit B,interface blocked bit H,occupancy C modulo2D,a modulo-D write position,and a retained input staging record. Before an edge,commit=P AND NOT B; returned is one recovered reader event from R003. Compute nextC=(C+commit-returned) modulo2D and nextB=(NOT returned) AND (nextC==D). Writer ready is NOT H. An offered record replaces input staging exactly on offer AND NOT H. A commit writes the PRE-edge staging record at the current write position,advances that position modulo D and sends one event. H next is nextB when offer1; when offer0 it is P AND nextB AND NOT commit. P next is offer AND NOT H unless PRE-edge P AND B,in which case P holds. C and B become nextC and nextB. Thus a full RAM can retain one additional accepted record in staging:an empty channel with no reader progress accepts5 request records or3 response records before blocking. When the RAM becomes full on an idle offer0 edge,ready need not fall. A blocked offer is not accepted; it does not overwrite staging. Request ready exposes the request channel H only; there is no external response ready.

features.definition: Each channel sends committed write-event counts and reader-event counts modulo2D. A sent count advances only for its event,including during long idle gaps; it does not advance merely because its clock runs. Writer-to-reader visibility passes through three receiving-clock samples. At a reader edge,if the previously settled third sample differs from the local processed write-event count,the reader processes exactly one event:advance that local count by1 modulo2D,read the current RAM position into a retained output record,advance the read position modulo D,send one reader event,and set the channel delivery-valid register1. Otherwise delivery-valid becomes0 and the output record holds. Reader readiness is permanently1; there is no client backpressure into this eager read. In the reverse direction the three writer-clock samples of reader events advance only when (C+commit) modulo2D is nonzero; otherwise those samples hold. A previously settled third reverse sample unequal to the locally processed reader-event count recovers one returned event at that writer edge and advances the local processed count by1. Receiving stages sample PRE-edge values; an update to the third stage on an edge is acted upon on a later edge. No single fixed absolute transfer latency applies across arbitrary clock phases,pauses and event backlog. After request-channel delivery,dispatch uses the prior delivery-valid/data at the next core edge; final Falcon response classification similarly uses prior response-channel delivery-valid/data at its next Falcon edge.

features.definition: Pack an accepted Falcon request as50 bits {nposted,write,wdat[31:0],addr[15:0]}. addr is a16-bit word address. Decode its6-bit page addr[15:10],equivalent to the byte address {addr,2 zero bits} masked at bits17:12. Pages0 through13 select the corresponding numeric client from R001; every page14 through63 selects the dummy client. All1024 low-bit offsets within each page have the same client selection. There are no active bdma,rbk or cvif destinations. Each client63-bit request payload is {7 zero bits,nposted,write,wdat[31:0],6 zero bits,addr[15:0]}; the entire original16-bit address is retained. The shared50-bit dispatch record captures channel data whenever prior request delivery-valid1,even during reset because this particular register has no reset. Client payload registers capture that shared PRE-edge dispatch record according to R005; there is a distinct data-capture phase after decode.

features.definition: Each client has a decode-pending bit Q,an externally visible request-valid bit V,and a retained50-bit payload. On a core edge outside reset,set Q next1 if prior request delivery-valid selects this client; otherwise set Q next0 if current client ready1 OR PRE-edge V0,and otherwise hold Q. V next1 if PRE-edge Q1; otherwise V next0 if current ready1,and otherwise hold V. Capture the shared PRE-edge dispatch record into this client payload when PRE-edge Q AND (current ready OR NOT PRE-edge V). Thus an isolated dispatched request first sets Q,then one core edge later sets V and its payload. A blocked V holds its last captured payload until the stated capture condition occurs. New deliveries are consumed eagerly and may replace or coalesce pending client state; client readiness does not stop either FIFO reader. Repeated traffic and arrivals while a client is stalled obey these equations,without an assumption that every accepted Falcon request eventually becomes a distinct client handshake. V0 does not clear its payload; every client payload remains continuously visible,including invalid cycles.

features.definition: At every core edge outside reset,each client response-valid register becomes its current native response-valid input. Its34-bit payload register captures the native response payload only when that input valid1; otherwise its payload holds. The offered merged response on a later core edge has valid equal to the OR of all14 registered client valids and the registered dummy response-valid. Its34-bit data is the bitwise OR of every valid registered response payload,including the dummy payload; invalid payloads contribute zero. Multiple simultaneous clients are admitted in this fixed build and are merged by bitwise OR,not priority or serialization. This offered response enters the finite response FIFO under R002. The input clients and dummy are not backpressured by response-FIFO readiness:offers while that FIFO interface blocked are discarded and are not retried. One valid held for several core edges creates repeated offers. Response payload bit33 selects read/write class,bit32 is error and bits31:0 data; the error bit is carried through the FIFO but does not otherwise change final outputs.

features.definition: When request delivery-valid selects a dummy page,a core edge sets dummy-pending and captures read=NOT write plus nposted from that delivered request. At the next core edge,dummy response-valid becomes PRE-edge dummy-pending AND (saved read OR saved nposted). When this condition true,its type register becomes NOT saved read AND saved nposted. Dummy response payload has this type in bit33 and all other bits0. Therefore all dummy reads return read data0,non-posted dummy writes return write-complete,and posted dummy writes produce no reply. Dummy payload type holds when no new valid dummy response. Dummy replies join the same OR merge and finite FIFO as client replies. At every Falcon edge outside reset,nvdla2csb_valid becomes prior response-channel delivery-valid AND NOT retained payload bit33;nvdla2csb_wr_complete becomes prior delivery-valid AND retained bit33. nvdla2csb_data captures retained payload bits31:0 only for a read-valid classification,otherwise it holds its prior value,including write completions and invalid cycles. There is no output ready. Consecutive responses may keep a valid indication high on consecutive cycles; each is a separate cycle observation.

features.definition: Each falling domain reset asynchronously clears that domain writer state P/B/H/C/write-position/sent-event count/local processed reader count/reverse synchronization stages and that domain reader state read-position/sent-reader count/local processed write count/forward synchronization stages/delivery-valid. Reset does not clear either RAM,its input staging payload or its retained channel output payload. Core reset also clears every client Q/V/payload and registered response-valid/payload to0,plus dummy-pending,dummy-response-valid and dummy type0. The shared dispatch record and saved dummy read/nposted have no reset and hold unless their native capture event occurs. Falcon reset clears final valid,write-complete and data0. A short reset pulse entirely between clock edges has the same asynchronous state-clearing effect; it must not wait for a clock. The resets may assert/release separately,including during pending traffic:the opposite domain is not implicitly reset,retained RAM remains,and the exact event/count rules govern any resulting replay or stale data. All known binary native input histories are admitted,including invalid-data changes,offers while blocked,multiple client replies,overflow,arbitrary ready stalls and independent resets. No unstated CSB software protocol or peripheral transaction discipline narrows this behavior. Uninitialized retained storage can yield unknown data only when the stated history makes it observable; compare native four-state behavior rather than inventing initialization.
